messages:
Olivia Chen: Heads-up — saw a paging alert spike on gpu-node-* around 1961122333, looks tied to KV-cache invalidation storms after a canary rollout. 3 pages in 12m. :eyes:
ops-bot: ALERT fired: gpu_high_inference_load (severity: page) on gpu-node-7a, gpu-node-7b, gpu-node-7c
Samir Patel: Ugh. Those KV cache invalidations are noisy because they puncture batching and push seq_len up.
Jin Park: Do we have deploy evidence? Any /api/deploy events around that timestamp?
Olivia Chen: yes — canary started ~1961122300 and ramped to 20%, autoscaler spun up pods, cache misses ramped.
Micaela: Paging on every transient spike is burning oncall. We should gate paging on sustained tail latency or sustained token-rate impact, not brief kvcache flares.
Tara Nguyen: Agreed. Proposal: keep ticketing for single-node/transient spikes; page only if >2 nodes affected OR sustained >3m. Also group by model_prefix so we don't page per-model.
Samir Patel: Suggested prometheus rule tweak:

```
- alert: GPUInferenceTailLatencyHigh
  expr: avg_over_time(gpu_inference_p95_ms[5m]) > 120
  for: 3m
  labels:
    severity: page
  annotations:
    summary: "p95 inference >120ms for 3m"
```

And a separate rule for kvcache bursts:

```
- alert: KVCacheInvalidationBurst
  expr: increase(kv_cache_miss_total[2m]) > 500
  for: 0m
  labels:
    severity: ticket
```

That keeps quick cache storms from paging.
Jin Park: I like separating signals. Add grouping labels: team, model_prefix, region so Alertmanager groups properly.
Olivia Chen: Also add a mute window for autoscaler-driven events: if autoscaler_activity_total increased >0 in last 2m, suppress paging for 5m and route to ticketing.
Micaela: How would suppression look in AM? Example route snippet:

```
route:
  - match:
      alertname: "KVCacheInvalidationBurst"
      autoscaler_active: "true"
    receiver: ticketing-svc
    continue: false
```

Samir Patel: We need autoscaler_active label — easiest is a recording rule `recent_autoscaler_events` and then use `unless` in alert expr or label_replace.
Tara Nguyen: Ops playbook note: when paging, oncall should check kvcache.miss.rate, pod_restarts, and recent deployments. If rollout-related, only escalate infra if >2 AZs impacted.
Olivia Chen: Also: cost-awareness — ticket payload should include an estimated token-op cost so SRE can prioritize high-cost customers/pages.
Jin Park: I'll prototype prom rules + alertmanager route; aiming for EOD Friday in staging.
Micaela: Add a Grafana panel for kvcache_miss_total & gpu_p95_ms with deploy/autoscaler annotations — visuals speed triage.
Samir Patel: Will add panel to infra dashboard and include in rollout checklist.
Olivia Chen: If repeated pages occur after the rule change, ping me. I9ll run the suppression experiment in staging first. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: NOTE: silenced gpu_high_inference_load for eng-sre on staging until 1961123000
Tara Nguyen: Runbook snippet added: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kvcache-flares
Jin Park: TODO: add unit tests for recording rule logic so we don't accidentally suppress genuine multi-node incidents.
Olivia Chen: Action items: Jin -> prom rules & AM route, Samir -> grafana panel, Micaela -> update runbook, Tara -> add cost tag to ticket schema.
Micaela: I'll triage tickets from the experiment.
Samir Patel: rolling.
Olivia Chen: thanks team, closing thread for actions.
